footnotes: According to Heyde*****, this was Fiebig's workshop symbol.

The figure of 33mm was obtained by dividing 44mm, the distance used to extend the slide for "first position" on the
tenor trombones (44mm) by 4/3, the ratio of a perfect fourth, which represents the difference in fundamental between
the Fiebig alto trombone and the tenors.
signature: On bell rim: "JOHANN CHRISTOPH FIEBIG MACHTS IN BERNGRUNDT 1771 (inscription somewhat carelessly done; letter "N" stamped backwards in every instance; other letters of varying sizes; many not positioned squarely); maker's mark: double fleur-de-lis.¹
pitch: E% + 30 cents @ a1 = 440 with slide closed; E% - 20 cents @ a1 = 440 with slide extended approx. 33mm.²
dimensions: bo 9.6, be 103, le 2001.5, int. diam of mouthpipe 11.3, int. diam. of slide receiver 10.4, int. diam. of bell receiver 11.9, ext. diam. of neckpipe at junction with first ferrule 11.8/12.4, ext. diam. of neckpipe at junction with bell- bow 12.4, ext. diam. of bell-pipe at junction with bell-bow 12.6, diam. of throat (140 mm from bell opening) 20.5, width of garland 20.5, length of air column in slide sec. (without mp) 1229, length of air column in bell sec. 772.5, overlap, slide sec. to bell sec. when assembled 41.5, conical portion 587 (=29%), mean thickness of bell .30.³
literature: Heyde 1980a, Sachs 1922 (regarding bell of bass trombone in Berlin collection); Stewart 1997.
remarks: Breathy sound; harmonics not in tune; probable air leak.Upper slide tube shows evidence of repair; slide tubes unequal in length prior to restoration; rings in slide bow and bell bow; lower slide stay telescopic; tubular slide stays, immovable stay dented, moveable stay telescopic; no slide stockings; rings in bell- and slide-bow, both made of thin strips of brass rather than wire; each ring attached to saddle; upper branch of inner slide shows repair: it is in two sections, upper 44.6mm, lower 380mm; inner slide tubes are of differing lengths as a result of this repair; bell-stay is more or less square in cross-section, soldered on nickpipe side, hinged on bell-pipe side, attached with a pin; rim-wire has cord or braid pattern; ferrules have ring pattern: each ferrule has four or five sets of rings; most of these sets are double; a few are triple. Dents in outer radius of slide bow; opened soft solder patch on front of bell sec. closed during restoration. Bell at 2nd pos. Bell-stay and immoveable slide-stay dented and apparently bent. Conservatively restored by Gary Stewart, 1997.
